subject: Escrow / Clawback options for multi-year prepay + renewal paths
messages:
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
To: Emily Thomas <emily.thomas@brightwellhealth.com>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.ai, vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 13 Dec 2026 10:02:00 -0500
Subject: Options for multi-year prepay — escrow vs. tiered refunds

Emily — great speaking this morning. Per our call, I wanted to outline two pragmatic approaches Brightwell can pick from for a 3-year prepay structure (you asked for language that plays nice with procurement/accounting):

1) Escrow-backed prepay (preferred for compliance teams)
   - Customer prepays Year1+Year2 in full into a third-party escrow account. Redwood recognizes revenue as services are delivered.
   - Early termination: funds remaining in escrow are returned to customer net of used consumption; Redwood provides consumption report and a 60-day clawback window for disputed consumption.
   - Refund timing: escrow admin returns funds within 30 days of termination.

2) Tiered refund + co-terming credit (preferred for simple accounting)
   - Prepay paid to Redwood; refund schedule embedded in contract:
     * Termination in Y1 => refund = 70% of remaining prepay; Y2 => 85%; Y3 (post-commit) => no refund.
     * Co-terming: if Brightwell co-terms additional workloads into the contract, we apply a prorated credit that reduces the early-exit exposure.

Attached: Brightwell_SOW_v3.pdf (SOW redline), prepay-refund-matrix.xlsx (illustrative numeric examples), redwood_prepay_cheatsheet.xlsx (internal ops notes).

Two asks: 1) Which approach would procurement prefer? 2) If escrow, do you have a preferred escrow vendor or do you want Redwood to propose one?

Thanks,
Sean
Sean Gallagher
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
From: Emily Thomas <emily.thomas@brightwellhealth.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>, marissa.cole@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@brightwellhealth.com
Date: Tue, 14 Dec 2026 09:17:00 -05:00
Subject: Re: Options for multi-year prepay — escrow vs. tiered refunds

Thanks, Sean — helpful summary. Procurement had a quick follow-up after reviewing the SOW:

- Procurement leans toward escrow for auditability but wants an explicit clawback matrix for how usage is calculated and dispute resolution timing (they asked for a 45-day resolution SLA).
- They also asked whether Redwood would accept a third-party escrow admin (we prefer that) and whether escrow fees are split.
- On the tiered refund approach, they requested concrete dollar examples and accounting treatment language to share with finance.

Can Redwood propose the escrow agreement (we can redline), and provide a firm example showing refunds at 6, 12, 18 months into a 36-month commitment? Also, any chance of softening the early termination refund in Y1 from 70% -> 60% if Brightwell commits to a minimum monthly throughput guarantee?

Emily Thomas
Director, Procurement
Brightwell Health
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>, vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai, rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 14 Dec 2026 10:45:00 -05:00
Subject: Fwd: Options for multi-year prepay — internal proposal

Team — forwarding Emily's note. My read: escrow is likely a blocker for finance unless we own the admin/fee flow or cap fees. Proposed internal counter:

- Offer Redwood-proposed escrow with fees split 50/50 on a one-time admin fee (we absorb first $2k, customer covers rest). Include language: Redwood provides monthly consumption statements; customer has 30 days to dispute. If dispute unresolved within 45 days, neutral arbiter (list of 3 firms) engaged — costs split.
- Refund matrix (we should provide exact $ examples). For simplicity, I recommend we:
   * Keep Tiered refund base as Sean proposed but make Y1 refund 60% if customer signs a Minimum Throughput Guarantee (MTG) of X tokens/month.
   * Add co-term credit table: when co-term added within first 12 months, apply a 10% credit to remaining prepay for each new product integrated (cap 30%).

Rishi — can you run the numbers on a $1.2M 3-year prepay (yearly equal tranches) and show: escrow refund flow, tiered refund flow, and MTG-adjusted refund? Vanessa — I expect you to draft the proposed escrow clause and a quick redline for the SOW.

Marissa
VP, Sales Operations
Redwood Inference
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 15 Dec 2026 09:30:00 -05:00
Subject: Re: Options for multi-year prepay — numbers and next steps

Attaching the requested matrix (prepay-refund-matrix.xlsx) and a short note:

Summary (numbers based on $1,200,000 3-yr prepay paid upfront):
- Escrow: If Brightwell terminates at 6 months, used consumption = $220k => escrow returns $980k minus escrow fee ($1.5k). Refund timeline 30 days after termination.
- Tiered refund (base): Termination in Y1 => 70% of remaining => $840k returned; Y2 => 85% => $510k; Y3 => 0.
- Tiered w/ MTG in place: Y1 refund improves to 60% of remaining (customer worse off), but we proposed 60% (i.e., they get $720k) only if MTG is met; otherwise revert to 70% base.

Recommended commercial language to move procurement:
- Redwood will propose an escrow administrator (we suggest Concord Escrow). Fees split 50/50; Redwood caps its payable fees at $2,000.
- Consumption reporting cadence: monthly; disputes raised within 30 days, resolved within 45 days; unresolved -> arbitration.
- Co-term credit: 10% credit applied to remaining prepay per additional product integrated within first 12 months (max 30%).

Next steps: Vanessa to send SOW redline with escrow clause + rationalized refund table. Sean to provide final doc and DocuSign link for signature if Brightwell selects one of the two approaches. I'll upload the full matrix to the HubSpot record (link above).

Rishi Malhotra
Director, Deal Economics
Redwood Inference
